body: # submission name: mask_decoder # upload zipped `archive.zip` [archive.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27271580/archive.zip) # report.txt ``` === Evaluation config === batch_size: 16 device: cuda num_threads: 2 prefetch_queue_depth: 4 report: submissions/mask_decoder/report.txt seed: 1234 submission_dir: submissions/mask_decoder/ uncompressed_dir: /home/ddbb/comma_video_compression_challenge_integration_qualitygpu/videos video_names_file: /home/ddbb/comma_video_compression_challenge_integration_qualitygpu/public_test_video_names.txt === Evaluation results over 600 samples === Average PoseNet Distortion: 0.00048759 Average SegNet Distortion: 0.00077435 Submission file size: 57,329 bytes Original uncompressed size: 37,545,489 bytes Compression Rate: 0.00152692 Final score: 100*segnet_dist + √(10*posenet_dist) + 25*rate = 0.19 ``` # does your submission require gpu for evaluation (inflation)? yes # did you include the compression script? and want it to be merged? no compression script, but did want it merged if it is a valid approach # additional comments I vibe coded too close to the Sun. I thought I worked with Codex to create an innovative solution building off the Quantizr mask approach, but then I saw https://github.com/commaai/comma_video_compression_challenge/pull/68 and realized I had just been moving bytes from the archive into my inflate.py. I was working on a write up of various solutions submitted to the competition, and why I thought mine was unique, but now I feel like this only contributes an exploit. I'll consider finishing the writeup this weekend since I still think it's a cool competition and the solutions so far have all been very cool.
